title: fix(qa): a wired realtime transport is admitted only by an `enforced` ledger row (#9083)
body:
Fixes #9083

## The defect

The ADR-0056 D10 authz conformance matrix carries a tripwire note promising that wiring an end-user realtime transport reds CI **"until this row is upgraded with the enforcement site."** The gate did not hold that out.

`checkLedger` requires an `enforcement` site only when `state === 'enforced'`, while a row's `covers` keys classify a discovered surface **regardless of state**. So the shortest path from red back to green was to append the tripwire key to the `experimental` `realtime-delivery-authz` row — a row whose own summary records that realtime fan-out has **NO** per-recipient authorization.

## Measured on `origin/main` `14c9ad71b`, before the change

The filer's two-leg reverse verification, re-run rather than inherited (their measurement was taken at `2cb69c31c`, many merges ago). Baseline: `Tests 15 passed (15)`.

**Leg 1** — wire a real transport (`const probe = new EventSource('/api/v1/stream');` in `packages/client/src/realtime-api.ts`):

```
AssertionError: UNCLASSIFIED surface — add a ledger row (ADR-0060): realtime:client/realtime-api.ts:transport(TRANSPORT-WIRED)
Tests  2 failed | 13 passed (15)
```

**Leg 2** — leave the transport wired, write **zero** authorization, append only the key to the experimental row's `covers`:

```
Tests  15 passed (15)
```

Green, with a live client transport and the matrix still recording "no per-recipient authorization". Both legs reproduce the filing exactly.

**Third measurement, not in the card.** `AuthzState` has a third member, and `removed` admits the identical exit: the same key on the `removed` `agent-visibility` row also returned `Tests 15 passed (15)`. The only thing `checkLedger` asks of a non-enforced row is a `note`. So the rule keys on **not `enforced`**, not on `experimental`.

## The change

`checkTransportWiredAdmission` in `authz-conformance.test.ts` refuses a `TRANSPORT-WIRED` key covered by any row that is not `enforced`. `checkLedger`'s existing enforced-has-site invariant supplies the other half, so the two **compose** into the promise the note makes — flipping a row's state without writing the site is refused as well (pinned as case (m)).

Three deliberate choices:

- **It lives beside the probe table, not in `checkLedger`.** `TRANSPORT-WIRED` is this ledger's own vocabulary, minted by the probe table 40 lines up. `checkLedger` is the shared ADR-0060 helper behind five other conformance ledgers, none of which has transport tripwires; teaching it this marker would leak one ledger's vocabulary into all of them. This also kept the change inside the declared file surface — `packages/verify/src/conformance.ts` is untouched.
- **Narrow, per triage's first option.** It keys on the tripwire marker only, not on `covers` in general — the broader "any row covering a `TRANSPORT-WIRED` key names a site regardless of state" was not adopted.
- **The marker cannot drift out of the rule's sight.** All five tripwire probes now mint their keys through one `tripwireKey()` helper, so a copy-pasted new tripwire is automatically in scope. The keys themselves are **byte-identical** to before — no churn, no baseline movement. Every assertion in the file now drives the composed `checkAuthzLedger`, so no case can pass against a weaker gate than the one CI runs.

## Reverse verification after the change

- **Leg 1 still reds**, same two cases, same message: `Tests 2 failed | 19 passed (21)`.
- **Leg 2 now stays red**: `Tests 8 failed | 13 passed (21)`, where it was `15 passed (15)`. The load-bearing failure names the row and the remedy:

```
realtime-delivery-authz: a TRANSPORT-WIRED surface cannot be classified by a 'experimental' row
— realtime:client/realtime-api.ts:transport(TRANSPORT-WIRED). A wired end-user transport is
admitted only by an `enforced` row naming its per-recipient delivery authorization site ...
```

Reporting the direction honestly: leg 2 produces **eight** failures rather than one, because the ablation mutates the real matrix that the new pinned cases and the non-vacuity case read from — so those fire too, by design. Both legs were re-run from the **committed** state.

## The note, and everything else that made the same claim

The defect here is declared-not-equal-to-enforced *in the note*, so shipping a stricter gate while leaving the prose describing something else would only move the discrepancy. Corrected: the row's note, the `covers` field TSDoc, the matrix header, the test header, and the `#2992 / ADR-0096 D4` block comment.

Two further sites outside the declared file surface make the same promise — `packages/spec/src/contracts/realtime-service.ts` ("so CI blocks it, not review") and `packages/services/service-realtime/README.md` ("fail CI if a transport is wired without upgrading that row with a real enforcement site"). Both were **false before this change and are true after it**, so they are left untouched rather than edited.

## Scope

Gate behaviour and prose only. No runtime, spec or product surface changes; **no matrix row changed state**, and no row's `covers` changed. Nothing was weakened to make CI green — the only new red the change can produce is the one it exists to produce.

Six new cases (21 total, was 15) pin the rule: both reverse-verification legs, the `removed` state, a non-vacuity check that the real matrix declares no `TRANSPORT-WIRED` key today, a positive control proving an `enforced` row naming its site **does** still admit the key (the gate is stricter, not impassable), and the composition case. Each refusal case additionally asserts that bare `checkLedger` accepts the very same ledger, so none of them can pass for an unrelated reason.

This becomes live work when #8347 (WS/SSE transport, v18) mounts a route — landing before that, not after.

## Verification

All at `786bd1c4e`, the final commit.

| Gate | Result |
|:--|:--|
| `@objectstack/dogfood` `vitest run authz-conformance conformance-helper` | `40 passed (40)` |
| `@objectstack/dogfood` `typecheck` | pass |
| `eslint --no-inline-config` on both changed files | pass |
| ESLint job family: `check:nul-bytes`, `check:slot-lookup`, `check:query-options-erasure`, `check:where-matcher`, `check:engine-double-contract`, `check:cross-package-test-inputs`, `check:verify-stand-in`, `check:authz-resolver`, `check:test-source-alias`, `check:type-source-resolution`, `check:changeset-gate-self-tests`, `check:objectui-changeset` | all pass |
| TypeScript Type Check job: `check:type-check-coverage`, `check:type-check-debt --re-measure` | pass (33 entries re-measured, none above its recorded number) |
| spec-liveness-check job: `check:empty-state`, `check:liveness`, `check:strictness-ledger`, `check:variant-docs` | all pass |
| docs-drift-check job: `check-affected-docs.mjs` | pass |

`check:type-check-debt` needed the full workspace build first (`turbo run build --filter=./packages/* --filter=./packages/*/*`); on an unbuilt tree it refuses outright, which is "not measured", not "passing".

Changeset included (`@objectstack/dogfood` patch).
